members.first_12: The (1,2) component of the first directional derivative in E1 is p*exp[x,y].
members.first_21: The (2,1) component of the first directional derivative in E2 is q*exp[x,y].
members.second_11: Equation (2.2) with the displayed A,E1,E2 gives the (1,1) mixed component p*q*exp[x,x,y].
members.second_22: Equation (2.2) with the displayed A,E1,E2 gives the (2,2) mixed component p*q*exp[x,y,y].

source_basis: Higham--Relton equation (2.2) defines the higher derivative as a mixed partial; Theorem 3.5 identifies it with a block of exp(X2). Coefficient extraction in the eigenbasis of diag(x,y) yields the listed divided-difference components. The package verifier certifies only the exact scalar reconstruction, not the general matrix theorem.
